title: Business Moguls
tagline: Men who turned skill into ownership. The exit matters — own the thing you build.

entries.name: Regis Prograis
entries.self_note: Boxers belong here because the hustle math is the same: skill + promotion + ownership.
entries.claim: Two-time junior-welterweight world champion from New Orleans who owns his own promotional company and speaks openly about fighters getting robbed by promoters who own their contracts.
entries.receipts: WBA (Super) title 2019, WBC title 2022. Prograis Boxing Promotions — he promotes his own cards in New Orleans. He has said in interviews that the reason he promotes himself is that fighters who sign everything away wake up broke in the same city they sold out.
entries.the_transfer: Regis owns his own promotion. That's the lesson in every PRICING.md rate floor in this repo: the whole FED-EDU hustle philosophy is 'don't sign your code away for exposure.' When you build a client site — $150 one-pager, $500 multi-page — the contract says YOU keep the code, the client gets the deliverable. Read the license before you sign. Own your promo.

entries.name: Daymond John
entries.claim: Sewed the first FUBU hats at his mother's house in Queens with a $40 budget, then turned FUBU into a global streetwear empire.
entries.receipts: FUBU: over $6 billion in lifetime sales. Started sewing hats between shifts at Red Lobster. Shark Tank investor since season one — over $8 million of his own money invested in founders, dozens of deals. The Power of Broke is his book about exactly the starting-with-nothing engine FED-Brother runs on.
entries.the_transfer: Daymond's mother took out a second mortgage on her house to fund his first production run — and he had already SOLD the hats before she did. Pre-sell before you build. Your $150 one-pager deposit rule comes from the same place: take half up front, build after the money clears. Never build on spec for strangers. Get the deposit.

entries.name: Robert F. Smith
entries.claim: Chemical engineer turned Goldman banker turned founder of Vista Equity Partners — the firm that buys and runs software companies worth billions.
entries.receipts: Vista Equity Partners: $100B+ in assets. Software companies under his model run on documented, repeatable process — the whole Vista playbook is standardization, the same discipline as your playbook. Morehouse Commencement 2019: he cleared the student debt of the entire graduating class — 396 men, ~$34 million — on stage, unannounced.
entries.the_transfer: Vista buys software companies and makes them better with PROCESS, not genius. That's this repo's whole bet: your first landing page is a documented, repeatable playbook you run for every client after it. You don't need to be a genius — you need to be repeatable. That's the billion-dollar lesson. Repeatable beats brilliant.

entries.name: Sean 'Diddy' Combs
entries.claim: Intern at Uptown Records who got fired, started Bad Boy out of anger, and built a music, fashion, liquor, and media empire on the back of one lesson: own the masters.
entries.receipts: Bad Boy Records: 75+ million records sold. Sean John: over $500M in sales, CFDA award. Cîroc partnership: he took a percentage deal instead of a flat fee and turned it into hundreds of millions. Three Grammy awards. Forbes list mainstay — at times the highest-paid musician in the world.
entries.the_transfer: Cîroc is the clearest case study in ownership economics for a coder. Diddy didn't invent vodka. He didn't build a distillery. He brought the audience and negotiated OWNERSHIP of the upside instead of a flat fee. When a client offers you $200 flat for a site, that's the flat fee trap — the site drives their revenue forever and you get paid once. Charge the retainer: $50/mo maintenance (PRICING.md). Equity thinking, freelancer prices.
entries.honest_note: Combs faces serious charges including sex trafficking and racketeering (2024 indictment, trial 2025). FED-EDU does not celebrate the man — we teach the ownership economics lesson from his career arc while stating plainly: the charges are real, the conduct is unacceptable, and owning your masters does not own your morals. Brothers should study the deal structure, not the man.
